verses.text: Before anything got started, the Word already was. The Word was with God, and the Word was God.
The Word was already there with God from jump.
Everything that exists came through him. Nothing got made without him.
Life was in him, and that life lit up humanity.
That light keeps shining in the dark, and darkness couldn’t shut it down. ✨
God sent a man named John onto the scene.
He came as a witness, speaking up about the light so everyone could believe through him.
John wasn’t the light, though. He came to point people to it.
The real light—the one shining on everyone—was coming into the world.
He was already in the world. The world came through him, but didn’t even recognize him.
He came to his own people, and they didn’t welcome him in.
But everyone who welcomed him, everyone trusting in his name, got the right to become God’s children.
They weren’t born from bloodline, human craving, or somebody’s plan; their birth came from God.
The Word became human and set up home among us. We saw his glory—the glory of the Father’s one and only Son, full of grace and truth.
John spoke up about him, calling out, “This is the one I meant when I said, ‘The one coming after me ranks ahead of me, because he was here before me.’”
Out of all that fullness, we’ve all received grace on top of grace.
Moses brought the Law, but grace and truth came through Jesus Christ.
No one has ever seen God—not once. The one and only Son, close to the Father’s heart, has made him known.
Here’s how John’s testimony went: Jewish leaders sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?”
He said it straight and didn’t deny it: “I am not the Christ.”
They pressed him: “Okay, then who? Elijah?” He said, “No.” “Are you the Prophet?” He answered, “No.”
They said, “So who are you? We need a straight answer for the people who sent us. What do you say about yourself?”
He said, “I’m a voice calling out in the wilderness: ‘Make the Lord’s road straight,’ just like Isaiah the prophet said.”
The people who had been sent were Pharisees.
They pressed him, “Then why are you baptizing if you’re not the Christ, Elijah, or the Prophet?”
John answered, “I baptize with water. But there’s someone standing right among you whom you don’t know.
He’s the one coming after me, but he ranks ahead of me. I’m not even worthy to untie his sandal strap.”
This all happened in Bethany, across the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
Next day, John saw Jesus coming his way and said, “Look—the Lamb of God, the one who takes away the world’s sin!
This is the one I meant when I said, ‘A man’s coming after me, but he ranks ahead of me because he was here before me.’
I didn’t know who he was, but I came baptizing with water so he could be revealed to Israel.”
John testified, “I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove and stay on him.
I didn’t know him, but the one who sent me to baptize with water said, ‘The one you see the Spirit come down and remain on is the one who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.’
I’ve seen it, and I’m telling you: this is the Son of God.”
Next day, John was back there with two of his disciples.
He saw Jesus walking by and said, “Look—the Lamb of God!”
The two disciples heard him and started following Jesus.
Jesus turned, saw them following, and asked, “What are you looking for?” They said, “Rabbi”—that means Teacher—“where are you staying?”
He said, “Come and see.” They went, saw where he was staying, and hung out with him that day. It was about four in the afternoon.
One of those two who heard John and followed Jesus was Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother.
Andrew went straight to find his brother Simon and told him, “We found the Messiah!” (That means Christ.)
He brought Simon to Jesus. Jesus looked at him and said, “You’re Simon, Jonah’s son. You’ll be called Cephas”—which means Peter.
Next day, Jesus decided to head for Galilee. He found Philip and said, “Follow me.”
Philip was from Bethsaida, the same town as Andrew and Peter.
Philip found Nathanael and told him, “We found the one Moses wrote about in the Law—and the prophets too: Jesus from Nazareth, Joseph’s son.”
Nathanael said, “Nazareth? Anything good really come from there?” Philip said, “Come and see.”
Jesus saw Nathanael coming and said, “Here’s a real Israelite—no fake in him!”
Nathanael asked, “How do you know me?” Jesus answered, “I saw you under the fig tree before Philip even called you.”
Nathanael said, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God! You are Israel’s King!”
Jesus answered, “You believe because I said I saw you under the fig tree? You’re about to see way greater things than that!”
Then he said, “I’m telling you the truth: you’ll see heaven opened and God’s angels going up and down on the Son of Man.” 🌌
Two days later, there was a wedding in Cana of Galilee. Jesus’ mother was there.
Jesus and his disciples had also been invited to the wedding.
When the wine ran out, Jesus’ mother said to him, “They’re out of wine.”
Jesus said to her, “Woman, why bring this to me? My time hasn’t come yet.”
His mother told the servants, “Do whatever he tells you.”
There were six stone water jars there, used for Jewish purification rituals. Each held about twenty or thirty gallons.
Jesus told the servants, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them all the way to the top.
Then he said, “Now scoop some out and take it to the head of the banquet.” They did.
The head of the banquet tasted the water that had become wine. He didn’t know where it came from, though the servants who had drawn the water knew. He called the bridegroom over
and said, “Everyone serves the best wine first. After the guests have had plenty, they serve the cheaper wine. But you’ve saved the best wine until now!”
Jesus did this, the first of his signs, in Cana of Galilee. He revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him.
After this, he went down to Capernaum with his mother, brothers, and disciples. They stayed there a few days.
The Jewish Passover was coming soon, so Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
In the temple courts he found people selling cattle, sheep, and doves, and money changers sitting at their tables.
He made a whip out of cords and drove them all out of the temple courts, including the sheep and cattle. He scattered the money changers’ coins and flipped over their tables.
He told the people selling doves, “Get these out of here! Don’t turn my Father’s house into a marketplace!”
His disciples remembered what Scripture says: “Passion for your house will consume me.”
The Jews responded, “What sign can you show us to prove you have the right to do this?”
Jesus answered, “Tear down this temple, and I’ll raise it up in three days.”
The Jews said, “This temple took forty-six years to build. You’re going to raise it up in three days?”
But he was talking about the temple of his body.
After he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered he had said this. Then they believed the Scripture and what Jesus had said.
While Jesus was in Jerusalem for Passover during the feast, many people believed in his name because they saw the signs he was doing.
But Jesus didn’t entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone.
He didn’t need anyone to tell him what people were like. He knew what was in every person.
There was a Pharisee named Nicodemus, one of the Jewish leaders.
He rolled up at night and told Jesus, “Rabbi, we know you’re a teacher sent from God. Nobody could do the signs you’re doing unless God was with him.”
Jesus answered, “I’m telling you straight: unless someone is born again, they can’t see God’s Kingdom.”
Nicodemus said, “How does an old man get born? He can’t climb back into his mom’s womb and start over, can he?”
Jesus answered, “I’m telling you straight: unless someone is born of water and the Spirit, they can’t enter God’s Kingdom.
A body gives birth to a body; the Spirit gives birth to spirit.
Don’t act shocked that I told you, ‘You all must be born again.’
The wind blows wherever it wants. You hear it, but you can’t tell where it came from or where it’s headed. That’s how it is with everyone born from the Spirit. 🌬️
Nicodemus asked him, “How can any of this happen?”
Jesus answered, “You’re Israel’s teacher, and this still isn’t clicking?
I’m telling you straight: we speak from what we know and testify to what we’ve seen, but you won’t accept our testimony.
If I tell you about earthly things and you don’t believe, how will you believe me when I tell you about heavenly things?
No one has gone up into heaven except the one who came down from heaven—the Son of Man, who is in heaven.
Just as Moses lifted up the snake in the wilderness, the Son of Man must be lifted up too,
so everyone who believes in him won’t perish, but will have eternal life.
God loved the world so much that he gave his one and only Son. Everyone who believes in him won’t perish but will have eternal life. ❤️
God didn’t send his Son into the world to judge it. He sent him so the world could be saved through him.
Whoever believes in him isn’t condemned. Whoever doesn’t believe has already been judged, because they haven’t trusted in the name of God’s one and only Son.
Here’s the judgment: light came into the world, but people chose darkness over light because their actions were evil.
Everyone doing evil hates the light and avoids it, so their actions don’t get exposed.
But whoever lives by the truth comes into the light, and it shows their actions were done through God.”
After that, Jesus and his disciples went into Judea. He stayed there with them and baptized people.
John was also baptizing at Aenon near Salim, because there was plenty of water there. People kept coming to get baptized.
This was before John was thrown into prison.
A debate broke out between John’s disciples and some Jews about purification.
They went to John and said, “Rabbi, that man who was with you across the Jordan—the one you testified about—is baptizing too, and everybody’s heading to him!”
John answered, “A person can receive nothing unless it’s given from heaven.
You heard me say it yourselves: ‘I am not the Christ. I was sent ahead of him.’
The bride belongs to the bridegroom. His friend stands nearby, listens in, and lights up when he hears the groom’s voice. That joy of mine is now complete.
He must grow greater; I must become less.”
“The one coming from above is over everybody. The one from earth belongs to earth and talks earthly talk. The one coming from heaven is over everybody.
He testifies to what he’s seen and heard, but no one accepts his testimony.
Whoever accepts his testimony puts their seal on this: God is true.
The one God sent speaks God’s words, because God gives the Spirit without limit.
The Father loves the Son and has put everything in his hands.
Whoever believes in the Son has eternal life. Whoever disobeys the Son won’t see life; God’s anger remains on them.”
Jesus heard the Pharisees had clocked he was making and baptizing more disciples than John.
To be clear, Jesus himself wasn’t baptizing people—his disciples were—
so he dipped out of Judea and headed for Galilee.
He had to pass through Samaria.
He reached a Samaritan town called Sychar, near the land Jacob had handed down to his son Joseph.
Jacob’s well was there. Jesus was worn out from the trip, so he sat down by the well. It was about noon.
A Samaritan woman came to draw water. Jesus asked her, “Could you get me a drink?”
His crew had gone into town to pick up food.
The woman said, “You’re a Jew, and I’m a Samaritan woman. Why are you asking me for a drink?” (Jews didn’t associate with Samaritans.)
Jesus answered, “If you knew what God gives—and who’s asking you for a drink—you’d ask him, and he’d give you living water.”
She said, “Sir, you don’t even have a bucket, and this well is deep. Where would you get this ‘living water’?
Are you greater than our ancestor Jacob, who gave us this well? He drank from it, and so did his kids and livestock?”
Jesus answered, “Everyone who drinks this water will get thirsty again.
But whoever drinks the water I give won’t thirst again—ever. It’ll become a spring inside them, flowing into eternal life.” 💧
The woman said, “Sir, give me that water, so I won’t get thirsty or have to keep making this trek here to draw water.”
Jesus told her, “Go call your husband and come back.”
She answered, “I don’t have a husband.” Jesus said, “That’s right—you don’t have a husband.
You’ve had five husbands, and the man you’re with now isn’t your husband. What you said is true.”
She said, “Sir, I can tell you’re a prophet.
Our ancestors worshiped on this mountain, but you Jews say Jerusalem is the place to worship.”
Jesus told her, “Believe me, the time is coming when you’ll worship the Father neither on this mountain nor in Jerusalem.
You worship what you don’t know; we worship what we know, because salvation comes from the Jews.
But the time is coming—and it’s already here—when true worshipers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. The Father is looking for people like that to worship him.
God is spirit, and the people who worship him must worship in spirit and truth.”
The woman said, “I know the Messiah is coming—the one they call Christ. When he gets here, he’ll explain everything to us.”
Jesus told her, “I am he—the one talking with you.”
Just then, his disciples came back. They were shocked he was talking with a woman, but nobody asked, “What do you want?” or “Why are you talking with her?”
The woman left her water jar, ran back into town, and told the people,
“Come meet a man who told me everything I’ve ever done. Could he be the Christ?”
They streamed out of town and started coming to Jesus.
Meanwhile, the disciples kept urging him, “Rabbi, please eat something.”
But he said, “I have food to eat that you don’t know about.”
The disciples said to each other, “Did someone bring him food?”
Jesus told them, “My food is to do what the one who sent me wants and finish his work.
Don’t you say, ‘Four more months till harvest’? I’m telling you, lift your eyes and check the fields—they’re already ripe for harvest.
The harvester gets paid and gathers a crop for eternal life, so planter and harvester can celebrate together.
So this saying is true: ‘One person plants; another comes along and harvests.’
I sent you to harvest what you didn’t work for. Others did the hard work, and you’ve stepped into their labor.”
Many Samaritans from that town believed in Jesus because of the woman’s report: “He told me everything I’ve done.”
When the Samaritans came to him, they begged him to stay. He stayed with them for two days.
Many more believed because of what he said.
They told the woman, “We believe now, not just because of what you said. We’ve heard him ourselves, and we know he really is the Christ, the Savior of the world.”
After those two days, Jesus left and went to Galilee.
Jesus himself had said that a prophet isn’t honored in his own homeland.
When he arrived in Galilee, the people welcomed him. They’d seen what he did in Jerusalem during the festival, because they’d been there too.
Jesus came back to Cana in Galilee, where he had turned water into wine. A royal official was there whose son was sick in Capernaum.
When the man heard Jesus had come from Judea to Galilee, he went to him and begged him to come down and heal his son, who was at death’s door.
Jesus told him, “Unless you people see signs and wonders, you won’t believe.”
The official said, “Sir, please come down before my child dies.”
Jesus told him, “Go on home. Your son lives.” The man trusted Jesus’ word and headed back.
As he headed down, his servants met him with the news, “Your child lives!”
He asked them when his son had started getting better. They said, “The fever left him yesterday at about one in the afternoon.”
The father realized that was the exact time Jesus had told him, “Your son is alive.” So he and everyone in his household believed.
This was the second sign Jesus did after coming from Judea to Galilee.
Some time later, during a Jewish festival, Jesus headed up to Jerusalem.
Near Jerusalem’s Sheep Gate was a pool called Bethesda in Hebrew, with five covered walkways.
A whole crowd of sick people was laid out there—blind, lame, and paralyzed—waiting for the water to move.
At certain times, an angel went down into the pool and stirred the water. The first person in after that was healed, whatever sickness they had.
One man there had been sick for thirty-eight years.
Jesus saw him lying there and clocked he’d been sick for a long time. He asked, “Do you want to get well?”
The man answered, “Sir, I have nobody to help me into the pool when the water moves. While I’m trying to get there, someone else slips in ahead of me.”
Jesus told him, “Get up, grab your mat, and walk.”
Right then, the man was healed. He picked up his mat and walked. And it was the Sabbath.
So the Jewish leaders said to the healed man, “It’s the Sabbath. The rules don’t let you carry that mat.”
He answered, “The man who healed me told me, ‘Grab your mat and walk.’”
They asked him, “Who told you, ‘Grab it and walk’?”
But the healed man didn’t know who it was. Jesus had slipped away into the crowd.
Later, Jesus found him in the temple and said, “Look, you’re well now. Stop sinning, or something worse may happen to you.”
The man went and told the Jewish leaders it was Jesus who had healed him.
That’s why the leaders came after Jesus and tried to kill him: he was doing these things on the Sabbath.
Jesus replied, “My Father is still working, and I’m working too.”
That only made them want to kill him more. He wasn’t just breaking the Sabbath; he called God his own Father and made himself equal with God.
Jesus answered, “I’m telling you straight: the Son can’t do anything on his own. He only does what he sees the Father doing. Whatever the Father does, the Son does too.
The Father loves the Son and shows him everything he does. He’ll show him even bigger works, and you’ll be amazed.
Just as the Father raises the dead and gives them life, the Son gives life to whoever he chooses.
The Father doesn’t judge anyone; he has given all judgment to the Son,
so everyone will honor the Son just like they honor the Father. Whoever disrespects the Son disrespects the Father who sent him.”
“I’m telling you straight: whoever hears my word and believes the one who sent me has eternal life. They won’t be judged; they’ve crossed over from death into life. 🌅
I’m telling you straight: the time is coming—and it’s already here—when the dead will hear the Son of God’s voice. Those who hear will live.
The Father has life in himself, and he gave the Son life in himself too.
He also gave the Son authority to judge, because he is the Son of Man.
Don’t be shocked by this. The time is coming when everyone in the tombs will hear his voice
and come out: those who did good will rise to life, and those who did evil will rise to face judgment.
I can do nothing on my own. I judge as I hear, and my judgment is right because I’m not chasing my own will, but the will of the Father who sent me.”
“If I testified about myself, my testimony wouldn’t stand.
Someone else speaks up about me, and I know his testimony about me is true.
You sent people to John, and he told the truth.
I don’t rely on human testimony, but I’m saying this so you can be saved.
John was a lamp, burning and shining bright, and for a while you were happy to enjoy his light.
But the proof I have tops John’s: the works the Father gave me to finish—the very works I’m doing—show that the Father sent me.
The Father who sent me has testified about me, but you’ve never heard his voice or seen his form.
His word isn’t living in you, because you don’t trust the one he sent.”
“You comb through the Scriptures because you think eternal life is in them. But they’re the ones pointing to me.
And still, you refuse to come to me to receive life.
I don’t take praise from people.
But I know you: God’s love isn’t in you.
I came in my Father’s name, and you won’t accept me. If someone comes in his own name, you’ll accept him.
How can you believe when you’re hyping each other up but don’t seek the praise that comes from the only God?”
“Don’t think I’m going to accuse you to the Father. Moses—the one you’ve put your hope in—is the one accusing you.
If you really believed Moses, you’d believe me, because he wrote about me.
But if you don’t believe what he wrote, how will you believe what I say?”
After that, Jesus crossed to the far side of the Sea of Galilee, aka the Sea of Tiberias.
A massive crowd was trailing him, because they’d seen the signs he did for sick people.
Jesus headed up the hillside and sat down there with his disciples. 🌄
Passover, the Jewish festival, was coming up.
Jesus looked up, saw the crowd coming his way, and asked Philip, “Where are we supposed to buy bread for all these people?”
He was putting Philip on the spot, but Jesus already knew what he was about to do.
Philip answered, “Even two hundred denarii worth of bread wouldn’t give everyone more than a little bite.”
Andrew, one of the disciples and Simon Peter’s brother, jumped in:
“There’s a kid here with five barley loaves and two fish. But come on, what’s that for this whole crowd?”
Jesus said, “Have everybody sit down.” There was loads of grass there, so the men settled in—about five thousand of them.
Jesus took the loaves and gave thanks. Then he handed them to his disciples to pass around. He did the same with the fish, giving everyone as much as they wanted.
When everybody had eaten their fill, Jesus told his disciples, “Gather up the leftovers. Don’t let anything go to waste.”
They scooped up the leftovers and filled twelve baskets with pieces from the five barley loaves the crowd had eaten. 🍞
When the people saw the sign Jesus had done, they said, “This really is the Prophet who was coming into the world!”
Jesus knew they were about to grab him and make him king by force, so he slipped back up the hillside alone.
When evening came, the disciples headed down to the sea.
They got into a boat and set off across the sea for Capernaum. It was dark, and Jesus still hadn’t joined them.
A strong wind kicked up, and the water got rough. 🌊
After rowing about three or four miles, they spotted Jesus walking on the sea and coming toward the boat. Fear hit them.
But he said, “It’s me. Don’t be scared.”
They welcomed him into the boat, and right away they reached the shore they were headed for.
Next day, the crowd still across the sea clocked that there had only been one boat. They knew Jesus hadn’t left with his disciples in it; the disciples had gone alone.
Some boats from Tiberias landed near the spot where the people had eaten the bread after the Lord gave thanks.
When the crowd realized Jesus and his disciples weren’t there, they hopped into the boats and went looking for him in Capernaum.
They found him across the sea and asked, “Rabbi, when did you get here?”
Jesus answered, “Real talk: you’re looking for me because you ate the loaves and got full, not because you saw the signs.
Don’t burn your energy chasing food that spoils. Work for the food that lasts into eternal life—the Son of Man will give it to you. God the Father has put his seal on him.”
They asked him, “So what should we do to carry out God’s work?”
Jesus answered, “Here’s God’s work for you: believe in the one he sent.”
They said, “Then what sign are you doing so we can see it and believe you? What work are you doing?
Our ancestors ate manna in the wilderness. Scripture says, ‘He gave them bread from heaven to eat.’”
Jesus told them, “I’m telling you straight: Moses didn’t give you the bread from heaven. My Father is the one giving you the true bread from heaven.
God’s bread is the one coming down from heaven and giving life to the world.”
They said, “Lord, keep that bread coming.”
Jesus told them, “I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to me won’t go hungry; whoever believes in me won’t be thirsty again.” 💛
But I’ve told you already: you’ve seen me, and you still don’t believe.
Everyone the Father gives me will come to me. Anyone who comes to me, I’ll never turn away—no way.
I came down from heaven to do my Father’s will, not to run my own agenda.
This is what my Father wants: I must not lose any of those he gave me; I’ll raise them up on the last day.
My Father wants everyone who sees the Son and believes in him to have eternal life. I’ll raise them up on the last day.”
The Jewish leaders started grumbling about Jesus because he said, “I am the bread that came down from heaven.”
They said, “Isn’t that Jesus, Joseph’s son? We know his parents. So how’s he claiming he came down from heaven?”
Jesus answered, “Quit grumbling among yourselves.
No one can come to me unless the Father who sent me draws them. I’ll raise them up on the last day.
The prophets wrote, ‘They’ll all be taught by God.’ Everyone who listens to the Father and learns from him comes to me.
No one has seen the Father except the one who comes from God. He has seen the Father.
I’m telling you the truth: whoever believes in me has eternal life.
I am the bread of life.
Your ancestors ate manna in the wilderness—and they died.
But here’s the bread coming down from heaven, so anyone can eat it and not die.
I am the living bread from heaven. Anyone who eats this bread will live forever. The bread I give for the world’s life is my flesh.”
The Jewish leaders started arguing with each other: “How can this man give us his flesh to eat?”
Jesus told them, “I’m telling you the truth: unless you eat the flesh of the Son of Man and drink his blood, you have no life in you.
Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood has eternal life, and I’ll raise them up on the last day.
My flesh is real food, and my blood is real drink—straight up.
Whoever eats my flesh and drinks my blood stays in me, and I stay in them.
The living Father sent me, and I live because of the Father. In the same way, whoever feeds on me will live because of me.
This is the bread that came down from heaven. It’s not like the manna your ancestors ate and then died. Whoever eats this bread will live forever.”
Jesus said all this while teaching in the synagogue at Capernaum.
A lot of his disciples heard him and said, “This teaching is tough. Who can even take it in?”
Jesus knew his disciples were grumbling about it. He asked, “Does this trip you up?
Then what if you saw the Son of Man going up to where he was before?
The Spirit is the one who gives life; the flesh gets you nowhere. The words I’ve spoken to you are spirit and life.
But some of you don’t believe.” Jesus knew from the start who didn’t believe and who would betray him.
He added, “That’s why I told you no one can come to me unless my Father grants it to them.”
After that, many disciples backed out and stopped following Jesus. 🚶
Jesus asked the Twelve, “You don’t want to leave too, do you?”
Simon Peter answered him, “Lord, who else are we going to? You have the words of eternal life.
We’ve come to believe and know you’re the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
Jesus answered them, “I chose you, all twelve, didn’t I? And one of you is a devil.”
Jesus was talking about Judas, Simon Iscariot’s son. Judas was one of the Twelve, but he was going to betray Jesus.
After that, Jesus kept it moving around Galilee. He wasn’t about to walk around Judea—the people there were looking to kill him.
The Jewish Festival of Booths was right around the corner.
So his brothers told him, “Leave here and head to Judea, so your disciples can see the things you’re doing too.
“Nobody does all this on the low if they want the whole world to know them. If you’re doing these things, show yourself to the world.”
Even his own brothers weren’t rocking with him yet; they didn’t believe in him.
Jesus told them, “My time hasn’t come yet. Your time? You can move whenever.”
“The world can’t hate you. It hates me because I tell it straight: its actions are evil.
“You go on up to the festival. I’m not going up just yet; my time hasn’t fully come.”
After saying that, Jesus stayed posted in Galilee.
But after his brothers went up to the festival, Jesus went too—quietly, not making a public entrance.
The Jewish leaders were looking around for him at the festival, asking, “Where is he?”
The crowd kept whispering about him. Some said, “He’s a good man.” Others said, “Nah, he’s leading the crowd astray.”
Still, nobody dared speak about him in the open—the Jewish leaders had them shook.
Halfway through the festival, Jesus went into the temple and started teaching. 📖
The Jewish leaders were shook: “How does he know the Scriptures like this when he never studied with our teachers?”
Jesus answered them straight: “What I teach isn’t my own; it comes from the One who sent me.”
“If anyone truly wants to do God’s will, they’ll know whether my teaching comes from God or whether I’m speaking on my own.
“Whoever is doing their own PR is chasing their own glory. But whoever seeks the glory of the One who sent him is true—no crookedness in him.”
“Didn’t Moses give you the Law? Yet none of you keeps it. So why are you trying to kill me?”
The crowd shot back, “You’ve got a demon! Who’s trying to kill you?”
Jesus answered, “I did one work, and all of you are still shook by it.
“Moses gave you circumcision—though it actually came from the ancestors, not Moses—and you circumcise a boy even on the Sabbath.
“If a boy can be circumcised on the Sabbath so Moses’ Law isn’t broken, why are you mad at me for making a whole man well on the Sabbath? Make it make sense.
“Stop judging by the outside. Judge with what’s right.”
Some people from Jerusalem said, “Isn’t this the man they’re trying to kill?”
“Look, he’s speaking openly and they’re letting him. Have the leaders decided he really is the Christ?”
“But we know where this man comes from. When the Christ shows up, nobody will know where he comes from.”
Then Jesus, teaching in the temple, called out, “So you know me and where I’m from? I didn’t come on my own. The One who sent me is real, but you don’t know him.
“I know him, because I’m from him, and he sent me.”
They tried to arrest him, but nobody laid a hand on him—his hour hadn’t come yet.
Still, many in the crowd believed in him. They asked, “When the Christ comes, will he really do more signs than this man has done?”
The Pharisees caught wind of the crowd murmuring about Jesus, so the chief priests and Pharisees sent temple officers to arrest him.
Jesus said, “I’m with you a little longer, then I’m going to the One who sent me.
“You’ll look for me but won’t find me. You can’t come where I’m going.”
The Jewish leaders wondered, “Where’s he planning to go that we won’t find him? Is he going to the scattered Jews living among the Greeks to teach the Greeks?”
“What does he mean, ‘You’ll look for me but won’t find me,’ and, ‘You can’t come where I’m going’?”
On the festival’s final, greatest day, Jesus stood up and called out, “If anyone’s thirsty, come to me and drink.
“Whoever believes in me—just as Scripture says—rivers of living water will flow from within them.” 💧
He was talking about the Spirit, whom believers in him would receive. The Holy Spirit hadn’t yet been given in this way, because Jesus hadn’t yet been glorified.
The crowd heard those words, and some said, “Yeah, this really is the Prophet.”
Others said, “He’s the Christ.” But some pushed back: “What, the Christ comes from Galilee?”
“Doesn’t Scripture say the Christ comes from David’s family and from Bethlehem, David’s town?”
And just like that, the crowd split into sides over him.
Some were ready to grab him, but nobody laid a hand on him.
The temple officers came back empty-handed to the chief priests and Pharisees. “Why didn’t you bring him?” they asked.
The officers said, “Nobody has ever talked like this man!”
The Pharisees snapped back, “So he fooled you too?”
“Name one ruler or Pharisee who’s believed in him?”
“But this crowd that doesn’t know the Law? They’re cursed.”
Then Nicodemus—the one who had gone to Jesus at night, one of their own—stepped in and spoke up:
“Does our Law judge a man before hearing him out and finding out what he’s done?”
They shot back, “Are you from Galilee too? Check the Scriptures: no prophet comes from Galilee.”
After that, everybody headed home.
But Jesus went to the Mount of Olives.
Early the next morning, he came back to the temple. All the people gathered around him, and he sat down to teach them.
The legal experts and Pharisees brought in a woman caught committing adultery. They made her stand right there in the middle.
They said to him, “Teacher, we caught this woman in the act of adultery.
Moses commanded us in the Law to stone women like this. So, what do you say?”
They were setting him up, hoping to get something they could use to accuse him. Jesus bent down and started writing on the ground with his finger.
They kept pressing him with questions. He stood up and said, “Let the one among you who has never sinned throw the first stone at her.”
Then he bent down again and kept writing on the ground.
When they heard that, their conscience hit them. One by one, starting with the oldest, they walked away. Jesus was left there alone with the woman still standing in the middle.
Jesus stood up and asked her, “Woman, where did they go? Did nobody condemn you?”
She said, “No one, Lord.” Jesus told her, “I don’t condemn you either. Go, and from now on, don’t sin anymore.”
Jesus spoke to them again: “I am the light of the world. Whoever follows me won’t walk around in darkness; they’ll have the light that gives life. 💡
The Pharisees challenged him: “You’re speaking for yourself. That testimony doesn’t count.”
Jesus answered, “Even if I speak for myself, my testimony is true. I know where I came from and where I’m going. You don’t know where I came from or where I’m going.
You judge by human standards. I don’t judge anyone.
And even when I do judge, my judgment is true, because I’m not alone. The Father who sent me is with me.
Your own Law says that the testimony of two people counts as valid.
I testify about myself, and the Father who sent me testifies about me.”
They asked him, “Where is your Father?” Jesus answered, “You don’t know me or my Father. If you knew me, you’d know my Father too.”
Jesus said these things while teaching in the temple treasury. Still, nobody arrested him, because his time hadn’t come yet.
Jesus told them again, “I’m going away. You’ll look for me, but you’ll die in your sins. You can’t come where I’m going.”
The Jewish leaders said, “Is he going to kill himself? Is that what he means by, ‘You can’t come where I’m going’?”
He told them, “You come from below; I come from above. You belong to this world; I don’t belong to this world.
I told you that you will die in your sins. Unless you believe that I am he, you will die in your sins.
They asked him, “Who are you, then?” Jesus answered, “I’ve been telling you from the start.
I have plenty to say about you and plenty to judge. But the One who sent me is true, and I’m telling the world what I heard from him.”
They didn’t realize he was talking to them about the Father.
So Jesus said, “When you lift up the Son of Man, then you’ll know that I AM. I do nothing on my own; I say what the Father taught me.
The One who sent me is with me. The Father hasn’t left me alone, because I always do what pleases him.”
While he was saying these things, many people believed in him.
Jesus said to the people who had believed him, “If you stay with my word, you’re really my disciples.
You’ll know the truth, and the truth will set you free.” 🔓
They answered, “We’re Abraham’s descendants. We’ve never been anybody’s slaves. So how can you say, ‘You’ll be set free’?”
Jesus answered, “I’m telling you the truth: everyone who keeps sinning is sin’s slave.
A slave doesn’t stay in the family home forever, but a son belongs there forever.
So if the Son sets you free, you’ll be free for real.
I know you’re Abraham’s descendants, but you’re trying to kill me because my word has no room in you.
I tell you what I have seen with my Father. But you are doing what you have seen with your father.”
They replied, “Abraham is our father.” Jesus said, “If you were Abraham’s children, you’d do what Abraham did.
But now you’re trying to kill me—a man who told you the truth I heard from God. Abraham didn’t do that.
You’re doing what your father does.” They said, “We weren’t born through sexual immorality. We have one Father: God.”
Jesus told them, “If God were your Father, you’d love me, because I came from God and I’m here. I didn’t come on my own; he sent me.
Why can’t you understand what I’m saying? It’s because you can’t bear to hear my word.

Your father is the devil, and you want to do what your father desires. He was a murderer from the beginning and does not stand in the truth, because there is no truth in him. When he lies, he speaks from his own nature: he is a liar and the father of lies.
But because I tell you the truth, you don’t believe me.
Which one of you can prove I’ve sinned? If I’m telling the truth, why don’t you believe me?
Whoever belongs to God hears God’s words. That’s why you don’t hear: you don’t belong to God.”
The Jewish leaders answered him, “Aren’t we right to say you’re a Samaritan and have a demon?”
Jesus replied, “I don’t have a demon. I honor my Father, and you dishonor me.
I am not chasing my own glory. There is One who seeks and judges.
I’m telling you the truth: whoever keeps my word will never see death.”
The Jewish leaders said, “Now we know you have a demon! Abraham died, and so did the prophets, but you say, ‘Whoever keeps my word will never taste death.’
Are you greater than our father Abraham, who died? The prophets died too. Who do you think you are?”
Jesus answered, “If I glorify myself, that glory is nothing. My Father is the one who glorifies me—the very one you claim as your God.
You don’t know him, but I do. If I said I didn’t know him, I’d be a liar like you. But I do know him, and I keep his word.
Your father Abraham was thrilled to see my day. He saw it and was glad.”
The Jewish leaders said to him, “You aren’t even fifty years old, and you’ve seen Abraham?”
Jesus said, “I’m telling you the truth: before Abraham came into being, I AM.”
So they picked up stones to throw at him. But Jesus slipped away and left the temple, passing right through the middle of them.
As Jesus was walking along, he saw a man who had been blind from birth.
His disciples asked him, “Rabbi, who sinned—this man or his parents—that he was born blind?”
Jesus answered, “It wasn’t that this man sinned, or that his parents did. This happened so God’s work could be shown in him.
While it’s still day, we must do the work of the One who sent me. Night is coming, when nobody can work.
As long as I’m in the world, I am the light of the world.”
After saying this, Jesus spat on the ground, made mud with the saliva, and spread it over the man’s eyes.
Then he told him, “Go wash in the pool of Siloam” (which means “Sent”). The man went, washed, and came back able to see. 👁️
His neighbors and the people who had seen him begging before started asking, “Isn’t this the man who used to sit and beg?”
Some said, “That’s him.” Others said, “No, he just looks like him.” But the man kept saying, “I’m the one.”
So they asked him, “How did your eyes get opened?”
He answered, “The man called Jesus made mud, spread it on my eyes, and told me, ‘Go to Siloam and wash.’ I went, washed, and now I can see.”
They asked him, “Where is he?” He said, “I don’t know.”
They brought the man who had been blind to the Pharisees.
The day Jesus made the mud and opened his eyes was the Sabbath.
So the Pharisees asked him again how he had received his sight. He told them, “He put mud on my eyes. I washed, and now I see.”
Some Pharisees said, “This man can’t be from God; he doesn’t keep the Sabbath.” Others said, “How could a sinner do signs like these?” They couldn’t agree.
So they asked the man again, “What do you say about him? He opened your eyes.” He said, “He’s a prophet.”
The Jewish authorities still refused to believe that he had been blind and had received his sight. So they called his parents
and asked them, “Is this your son, the one you say was born blind? How can he see now?”
His parents answered, “We know this is our son, and we know he was born blind.
But we don’t know how he can see now, or who opened his eyes. He’s old enough to answer for himself. Ask him.”
His parents said this because they were afraid of the Jewish authorities. The authorities had already agreed that anyone who confessed Jesus as the Messiah would be kicked out of the synagogue.
That’s why his parents said, “He’s old enough. Ask him.”
So they called the man who had been blind in again and said, “Give glory to God. We know this man is a sinner.”
He answered, “I don’t know whether he’s a sinner. Here’s what I do know: I was blind, and now I can see.”
They asked him again, “What did he do to you? How did he open your eyes?”
He replied, “I already told you, and you didn’t listen. Why do you want to hear it again? You want to become his disciples too?”
They insulted him: “You’re his disciple. We’re Moses’ disciples.
We know God spoke to Moses. But we don’t even know where this man comes from.”
The man answered, “Now that is wild! You don’t know where he comes from, yet he opened my eyes.
We know God doesn’t listen to sinners. But if someone worships God and does what he wants, God listens to that person.
From the beginning of the world, nobody has ever heard of anyone opening the eyes of someone born blind.
If this man weren’t from God, he couldn’t do anything.”
They shot back, “You were born steeped in sin, and now you’re trying to teach us?” Then they threw him out.
Jesus heard they had thrown the man out. When he found him, he asked, “Do you believe in the Son of God?”
The man answered, “Who is he, sir? Tell me, so I can believe in him.”
Jesus said, “You’ve seen him. He’s the one speaking with you now.”
The man said, “Lord, I believe!” Then he worshiped Jesus.
Jesus said, “I came into this world for judgment: so those who do not see may see, and those who see may become blind.”
Some Pharisees who were there heard him and asked, “Are you saying we’re blind too?”
Jesus answered, “If you were blind, you wouldn’t be guilty of sin. But you say, ‘We see,’ so your sin remains.”
“I’m telling you the truth: anyone who sneaks into the sheep pen some other way instead of coming through the gate is a thief and a robber.
The one who comes in through the gate is the shepherd of the sheep.
The gatekeeper opens for him. The sheep hear his voice; he calls his own sheep by name and leads them out.
When he has brought his own sheep out, he walks ahead of them. They follow because they recognize his voice. 🐑
They won’t follow a stranger. They’ll run from him, because a stranger’s voice is unfamiliar to them.”
Jesus told them this story, but they didn’t get what he meant.
So Jesus explained again: “I’m telling you the truth: I am the gate for the sheep.
All those who came before me are thieves and robbers, but the sheep did not listen to them.
I am the gate. Anyone who comes in through me will be saved. They’ll come and go and find good pasture.
A thief comes only to steal, kill, and destroy. I came so they could have life—life overflowing. ✨
“I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd lays down his life for the sheep.
A hired worker isn’t the shepherd and doesn’t own the sheep. When he sees a wolf coming, he leaves the sheep and runs. Then the wolf snatches them and scatters the flock.
He runs because he’s only there for the pay and doesn’t really care about the sheep.
I am the good shepherd. I know my own, and they know me—
just as the Father knows me and I know the Father. I lay down my life for the sheep.
I have other sheep that don’t belong to this sheep pen. I have to bring them too. They’ll hear my voice, and there will be one flock with one shepherd.
The Father loves me because I lay down my life so I can take it up again.
No one takes it from me. I lay it down by my own choice. I have authority to lay it down, and authority to take it up again. This is the command I received from my Father.”
These words caused another split among the Jewish leaders.
Many of them said, “He has a demon and he’s out of his mind! Why are you listening to him?”
Others said, “Those aren’t the words of someone with a demon. Could a demon open the eyes of a blind person?”
The Festival of Dedication was happening in Jerusalem.
It was winter, and Jesus was walking in the temple area, in Solomon’s Colonnade.
The Jewish leaders gathered around him and said, “How long will you keep us guessing? If you’re the Messiah, say it plainly.”
Jesus answered, “I already told you, but you don’t believe me. The works I do in my Father’s name speak for me.
But you don’t believe because you aren’t among my sheep, as I told you.
My sheep hear my voice. I know them, and they follow me.
I give them eternal life. They will never perish, and no one can snatch them out of my hand.
My Father, who gave them to me, is greater than all. No one can snatch them from the hand of my Father.
I and the Father are one.”
The Jewish leaders picked up stones again, ready to stone him.
Jesus said to them, “I’ve shown you many good works from my Father. Which one of those works are you stoning me for?”
They answered, “We’re not stoning you for a good work. We’re stoning you for blasphemy: you’re only a man, yet you make yourself God.”
Jesus replied, “Doesn’t your Law say, ‘I said, you are gods’?
If Scripture called those people ‘gods’—the ones who received God’s word—and Scripture can’t be undone,
why are you calling the one the Father set apart and sent into the world a blasphemer because I said, ‘I am the Son of God’?
If I’m not doing the works of my Father, don’t believe me.
But if I am doing them, even if you do not believe me, believe the works. Then you may know and believe that the Father is in me, and I am in the Father.”
They tried to seize him again, but he slipped away from them.
Jesus crossed the Jordan again and went to the place where John had first been baptizing. He stayed there.
Many people came to him. They said, “John didn’t perform any signs, but everything John said about this man was true.”
And many people there believed in him.
A man named Lazarus from Bethany was sick. Bethany was the village where Mary and her sister Martha lived.
Mary was the one who had anointed the Lord with perfume and wiped his feet with her hair. Her brother Lazarus was sick.
So the sisters sent Jesus a message: “Lord, the one you love is sick.”
When Jesus heard, he said, “This sickness won’t end in death. It will show God’s glory, and God’s Son will be glorified through it.”
Jesus loved Martha, her sister, and Lazarus.
So when he heard Lazarus was sick, he stayed where he was for two more days.
After that, he told the disciples, “Let’s go back to Judea.”
The disciples said, “Rabbi, the Jewish leaders were just trying to stone you. And now you want to go back there?”
Jesus answered, “Doesn’t the day have twelve hours of daylight? If someone walks in daylight, they don’t stumble, because they can see by this world’s light.
But if someone walks at night, they stumble, because there’s no light in them.”
Then he told them, “Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep. I’m going there to wake him up.”
The disciples said, “Lord, if he’s asleep, he’ll get better.”
They thought Jesus meant ordinary sleep. But he was talking about Lazarus’s death.
So Jesus told them plainly, “Lazarus is dead.
For your sake, I’m glad I wasn’t there, so you can believe. Now, let’s go to him.”
Thomas, also called Didymus, said to the other disciples, “Let’s go too, so we can die with him.”
When Jesus arrived, Lazarus had already been in the tomb for four days.
Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen stadia away.
Many people had come from the area to comfort Martha and Mary over their brother.
When Martha heard Jesus was coming, she went out to meet him. Mary stayed inside.
Martha said to Jesus, “Lord, if you had been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.
Even now, I know God will give you whatever you ask.”
Jesus said to her, “Your brother will rise again.”
Martha answered, “I know he’ll rise again when everyone is raised on the last day.”
Jesus said to her, “I am the resurrection and the life. Whoever believes in me will live, even if they die.
Everyone who lives and believes in me will never die. Do you believe this?”
She said, “Yes, Lord. I believe you are the Messiah, God’s Son—the one who was coming into the world.”
After saying this, Martha went back and quietly called her sister Mary. “The Teacher is here,” she told her, “and he is calling for you.”
When Mary heard, she got up quickly and went to him.
Jesus had not yet entered the village. He was still where Martha had met him.
The people who were in the house comforting Mary saw her get up quickly and leave. They followed, thinking she was going to the tomb to weep there.
When Mary reached Jesus and saw him, she fell at his feet. “Lord, if you had been here, my brother wouldn’t have died.”
Jesus saw her weeping, and saw the people who came with her weeping too. Deeply moved, he was troubled.
He asked, “Where have you laid him?” They said, “Lord, come and see.”
Jesus wept.
The people said, “Look how much he loved him.”
But some said, “Couldn’t the man who opened the blind man’s eyes have kept Lazarus from dying?”
Jesus was deeply moved again as he came to the tomb. It was a cave, with a stone covering the entrance.
“Move the stone,” Jesus said. Martha, the dead man’s sister, said, “Lord, there’ll be a smell by now. He’s been dead four days.”
Jesus said to her, “Didn’t I tell you that if you believed, you would see God’s glory?”
So they moved the stone. Jesus looked up and said, “Father, thank you for hearing me.
I know you always hear me. I said this because of the crowd standing here, so they may believe that you sent me.”
Then Jesus called out loudly, “Lazarus, come out!”
The man who had died came out, his hands and feet wrapped in burial cloths, and his face covered with a cloth. Jesus told them, “Unwrap him and let him go.”
Many of the people who had come to visit Mary saw what Jesus did and believed in him.
But some went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
So the chief priests and Pharisees called a council meeting. “What are we going to do?” they said. “This man keeps doing signs.
If we leave him alone like this, everyone will believe in him. Then the Romans will come and take away both our place and our nation.”
One of them, Caiaphas, was high priest that year. He said, “You don’t know what you’re talking about.
You haven’t thought this through: it’s better for us if one man dies for the people, instead of the whole nation being destroyed.”
He didn’t say this just on his own. Because he was high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus would die for the nation—
and not only for that nation, but to gather God’s scattered children together as one.
From that day on, they made plans to kill Jesus.
So Jesus stopped moving around openly among the Jewish authorities. He left for the region near the wilderness, to a town called Ephraim, and stayed there with his disciples.
The Jewish Passover was coming soon. Many people went up from the countryside to Jerusalem before Passover to purify themselves.
They looked for Jesus in the temple and asked one another, “What do you think? Is he not coming to the festival?”
The chief priests and Pharisees had ordered that anyone who knew where Jesus was must report it, so they could arrest him.
Six days before Passover, Jesus came to Bethany, where Lazarus lived—the man Jesus had raised from the dead.
They hosted a dinner for Jesus there. Martha served the meal, and Lazarus was among those sitting at the table with him.
Mary brought about a pound of expensive pure nard perfume, poured it on Jesus’ feet, and wiped his feet with her hair. The whole house filled with its fragrance. 🌿
Then Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son—one of Jesus’ disciples, the one who would betray him—said,
“Why didn’t we sell this perfume for three hundred denarii and give the money to the poor?”
He didn’t say that because he cared about the poor. He was a thief who kept the money bag and used to take what people put in it.
Jesus said, “Leave her alone. She kept this for the day of my burial.
You’ll always have the poor with you, but you won’t always have me.”
A large crowd of Jewish people heard that Jesus was there. They came not only because of Jesus, but to see Lazarus too—the man he had raised from the dead.
So the chief priests also made plans to kill Lazarus,
because many people were turning away and believing in Jesus because of him.
The next day, a huge crowd that had come for the festival heard Jesus was on his way to Jerusalem.
They took palm branches and went out to meet him, shouting, “Hosanna! Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord—the King of Israel!” 🌴
Jesus found a young donkey and sat on it, just as Scripture says:
“Don’t be afraid, daughter of Zion. Look—your King is coming, sitting on a donkey’s colt.”
At first his disciples didn’t understand what was happening. But after Jesus was glorified, they remembered that Scripture had said these things about him, and that people had done them to him.
The crowd that had been with Jesus when he called Lazarus out of the tomb and raised him from the dead kept telling people what they had seen.
That was why the crowd went out to meet Jesus: they had heard he had done this sign.
The Pharisees said to each other, “See? We’re getting nowhere. Look, the whole world has gone after him.”
Some Greeks were there among those who had come to worship at the festival.
They went to Philip, who was from Bethsaida in Galilee, and asked him, “Sir, we want to see Jesus.”
Philip went and told Andrew. Then Andrew and Philip went and told Jesus.
Jesus answered them, “The time has come for the Son of Man to be glorified.
I am telling you the truth: unless a grain of wheat falls into the ground and dies, it remains by itself. But if it dies, it produces much fruit. 🌾
Anyone who loves their life will lose it. Whoever hates their life in this world will keep it for eternal life.
If anyone serves me, they must follow me. My servant will be where I am. The Father will honor anyone who serves me.
“Now my soul is troubled. What should I say? ‘Father, save me from this hour’? But this is the very reason I came to this hour.
Father, bring glory to your name!” Then a voice came from heaven: “I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again.”
The crowd standing there heard it and said, “That was thunder.” Others said, “An angel spoke to him.”
Jesus answered, “That voice came for your sake, not mine.
Now this world is being judged. Now the ruler of this world will be thrown out.
And when I am lifted up from the earth, I will draw everyone to myself.”
He said this to show what kind of death he was going to die.
The crowd answered him, “We’ve heard from the Law that the Messiah remains forever. So how can you say the Son of Man must be lifted up? Who is this Son of Man?”
Jesus told them, “The light will be with you only a little longer. Walk while you have the light, so darkness doesn’t overtake you. Whoever walks in darkness doesn’t know where they’re going.
While you have the light, believe in the light, so you can become children of light.” After saying this, Jesus left and hid from them.
Even though Jesus had done so many signs right in front of them, they still didn’t believe in him.
This happened to fulfill the word of the prophet Isaiah: “Lord, who has believed our report? To whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed?”
That’s why they couldn’t believe. Isaiah also said:
“He has blinded their eyes and hardened their hearts, so they might not see with their eyes, understand with their hearts, turn back, and I would heal them.”
Isaiah said this because he saw Jesus’ glory and spoke about him.
Even so, many rulers believed in Jesus. But because of the Pharisees, they wouldn’t admit it; they were afraid of being put out of the synagogue.
They loved human praise more than praise from God.
Jesus called out, “Whoever believes in me believes not only in me, but in the One who sent me.
Whoever sees me sees the One who sent me.
I came into the world as light, so that whoever believes in me won’t stay in darkness.
If anyone hears what I say and does not believe, I do not judge that person. I did not come to judge the world; I came to save the world.
There is a judge for the one who rejects me and doesn’t accept what I say: the message I spoke will judge that person on the last day.
I did not speak on my own. The Father who sent me gave me a command about what I should say and what I should speak.
I know that his command is eternal life. So whatever I speak, I say just as the Father told me.”
Before the Passover festival, Jesus knew his time had come to leave this world and go to the Father. He had loved his own people in the world, and he loved them all the way through.
Dinner was underway. The devil had already put the idea of betraying Jesus into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son.
Jesus knew the Father had put everything into his hands, and that he had come from God and was going back to God.
So he got up from the meal, took off his outer clothes, and wrapped a towel around his waist.
Then he poured water into a basin and began washing the disciples’ feet, drying them with the towel around him. 💧
When he came to Simon Peter, Peter asked, “Lord, you’re going to wash my feet?”
Jesus answered, “You don’t understand what I’m doing right now, but you’ll understand later.”
Peter said, “You will never wash my feet!” Jesus replied, “If I don’t wash you, you have no share with me.”
Simon Peter said, “Lord, then wash my hands and head too—not just my feet!”
Jesus said, “Someone who has bathed only needs their feet washed; they’re already clean all over. You are clean, but not all of you.”
Jesus knew who was going to betray him. That was why he said, “Not all of you are clean.”
After washing their feet, Jesus put his outer clothes back on and sat down again. “Do you understand what I’ve done for you?” he asked.
“You call me ‘Teacher’ and ‘Lord,’ and you’re right—that’s who I am.
So if I, your Lord and Teacher, washed your feet, you should wash one another’s feet too.
I’ve given you an example. Do for each other what I’ve done for you.
I’m telling you the truth: a servant isn’t greater than the master, and a messenger isn’t greater than the one who sent them.
Now that you know this, you’ll be blessed if you put it into practice.
I’m not talking about all of you. I know the people I chose. But Scripture must come true: ‘The one who shares my bread has turned against me.’
I’m telling you this before it happens, so when it does happen, you’ll believe that I am he.
I’m telling you the truth: whoever welcomes someone I send welcomes me; and whoever welcomes me welcomes the One who sent me.”
After saying this, Jesus was deeply troubled. He told them plainly, “I’m telling you the truth: one of you will betray me.”
The disciples looked at one another, confused about who he meant.
One of the disciples Jesus loved was at the table, leaning against his chest.
Simon Peter gestured to him and said, “Ask him who he means.”
So that disciple leaned back toward Jesus and asked, “Lord, who is it?”
Jesus answered, “It’s the one I give this piece of bread to after I dip it.” Then he dipped the bread and gave it to Judas, Simon Iscariot’s son.
After Judas took the bread, Satan entered him. Jesus said to him, “What you’re going to do, do quickly.”
Nobody else at the table understood why Jesus said that to him.
Some thought that, since Judas kept the money bag, Jesus was telling him, “Buy what we need for the festival,” or to give something to the poor.
Judas took the bread and went out right away. It was night.
When Judas had gone, Jesus said, “Now the Son of Man is glorified, and God is glorified in him.
If God is glorified in him, God will also glorify him in himself—and do it right away.
Children, I will be with you only a little longer. You will look for me. As I told the Jewish leaders, you cannot come where I am going; now I tell you the same.
Here’s a new command I’m giving you: love one another. Love each other the way I have loved you. ❤️
Everyone will know you’re my disciples by this: you love one another.”
Simon Peter asked him, “Lord, where are you going?” Jesus answered, “You can’t follow me now, but you will follow later.”
Peter said, “Lord, why can’t I follow you now? I’ll give my life for you.”
Jesus answered, “You’ll give your life for me? I’m telling you the truth: the rooster won’t crow until you’ve denied me three times.”
“Don’t let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, and believe in me too.
There are many rooms in my Father’s house. If that weren’t true, I would’ve told you. I’m going there to prepare a place for you.
And if I go and prepare a place for you, I’ll come back and bring you to be with me, so you can be where I am.
You know where I’m going, and you know the way there.”
Thomas said to him, “Lord, we don’t know where you’re going. How can we know the way?”
Jesus said, “I am the way, the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.
If you really knew me, you’d know my Father too. From now on, you do know him and have seen him.”
Philip said, “Lord, show us the Father. That’s all we need.”
Jesus said to him, “Philip, have I been with you all this time and you still don’t know me? Whoever has seen me has seen the Father. So why ask, ‘Show us the Father’?
Don’t you believe that I am in the Father and the Father is in me? The words I tell you aren’t from me. The Father living in me is doing his work.
Believe me when I say I am in the Father and the Father is in me. Or at least believe because of the works themselves.
I’m telling you the truth: Whoever believes in me will do the works I’ve been doing. They’ll do even greater works, because I’m going to the Father.
Whatever you ask in my name, I’ll do it, so the Father may be glorified through the Son.
If you ask me for anything in my name, I’ll do it.
“If you love me, keep my commands.
I’ll ask the Father, and he’ll give you another Helper to be with you forever:
the Spirit of truth. The world can’t receive him because it doesn’t see or know him. You know him, because he stays with you and will be in you.
I won’t leave you like orphans. I’ll come to you.
In just a little while, the world won’t see me anymore, but you will see me. Because I live, you will live too.
When that day comes, you’ll know I am in my Father, you are in me, and I am in you.
Whoever has my commands and keeps them is the one who loves me. Whoever loves me will be loved by my Father. I’ll love them too and show myself to them.”
Judas—not Judas Iscariot—said to him, “Lord, why are you going to show yourself to us and not to the world?”
Jesus answered, “Anyone who loves me will keep my word. My Father will love them, and we will come to them and make our home with them.
Anyone who doesn’t love me won’t keep my words. The word you hear isn’t mine; it comes from the Father who sent me.
“I’ve told you these things while I’m still with you.
But the Helper, the Holy Spirit, whom the Father will send in my name, will teach you everything and remind you of all I’ve told you.
I leave you peace. I give you my peace, not the way the world gives it. Don’t let your hearts be troubled or afraid.
You heard me say, ‘I’m going away, and I’ll come back to you.’ If you loved me, you’d be glad I’m going to the Father, because the Father is greater than I am.
I’ve told you this before it happens, so that when it does happen, you’ll believe.
I won’t talk with you much longer, because the ruler of this world is coming. He has no hold over me.
But the world must know that I love the Father and do exactly what the Father commanded me. Get up; let’s leave this place.
“I am the true vine, and my Father is the gardener.
He cuts off every branch in me that doesn’t bear fruit. He prunes every branch that does bear fruit, so it can produce even more.
You’ve already been pruned clean because of the word I’ve spoken to you.
Stay in me, and I’ll stay in you. A branch can’t produce fruit on its own; it has to stay connected to the vine. Neither can you, unless you stay in me.
I am the vine; you are the branches. Whoever stays in me, and I in them, produces much fruit. Apart from me, you can do nothing.
If anyone doesn’t stay in me, they’re thrown away like a branch and dry up. People gather those branches, throw them into the fire, and burn them.
If you stay in me and my words stay in you, ask for whatever you want, and it will be done for you.
“My Father is glorified when you produce lots of fruit and show that you’re my disciples.
Just as the Father has loved me, I have loved you. Stay in my love.
If you keep my commands, you’ll stay in my love, just as I’ve kept my Father’s commands and stay in his love.
I’ve told you these things so my joy may be in you and your joy may be complete.
“This is my command: Love one another just as I have loved you.
No one has greater love than this: to give their life for their friends.
You are my friends if you do what I command you.
I no longer call you servants, because a servant doesn’t know what the master is doing. I’ve called you friends, because I’ve told you everything I heard from my Father.
You didn’t choose me; I chose you and appointed you to go and produce lasting fruit. Then the Father will give you whatever you ask in my name.
“I’m commanding you to love one another.
If the world hates you, remember it hated me first.
If you belonged to the world, it would love you as its own. But you don’t belong to the world. I chose you out of it, and that’s why the world hates you.
Remember what I told you: ‘A servant isn’t greater than the master.’ If they persecuted me, they’ll persecute you too. If they kept my word, they’ll keep yours too.
They’ll do all this to you because of my name, since they don’t know the one who sent me.
If I hadn’t come and spoken to them, they wouldn’t be guilty in this way. But now they have no excuse for their sin.
Whoever hates me also hates my Father.
If I hadn’t done among them works no one else has done, they wouldn’t be guilty in this way. But now they’ve seen the works and still hate both me and my Father.
This happened so the words written in their Law would be fulfilled: ‘They hated me without a reason.’
“When the Helper comes—the Spirit of truth, whom I’ll send to you from the Father—he will testify about me.
And you will testify too, because you’ve been with me from the beginning.
“I’ve told you these things so you won’t fall away.
They’ll put you out of the synagogues. The time is coming when anyone who kills you will think they’re serving God.
They’ll do these things because they haven’t known the Father or me.
I’ve told you this so that when the time comes, you’ll remember I warned you. I didn’t tell you from the beginning because I was with you.
But now I’m going to the one who sent me, and none of you asks me, ‘Where are you going?’
Because I’ve told you this, sadness has filled your hearts.
But I’m telling you the truth: It’s better for you that I go away. If I don’t go, the Helper won’t come to you. But if I go, I’ll send him to you.
When he comes, he’ll show the world what sin, righteousness, and judgment mean:
sin, because people don’t believe in me;
righteousness, because I’m going to the Father and you won’t see me anymore;
and judgment, because the ruler of this world has been judged.
“I still have many things to tell you, but you can’t handle them right now.
When the Spirit of truth comes, he’ll guide you into all truth. He won’t speak on his own; he’ll say what he hears and tell you what’s coming.
He’ll glorify me, because he’ll take what belongs to me and make it known to you.
Everything the Father has belongs to me. That’s why I said the Spirit will take what’s mine and make it known to you.
“In a little while, you won’t see me anymore. Then, after a little while, you’ll see me again.”
Some of his disciples said to one another, “What does he mean by, ‘In a little while you won’t see me, and then after a little while you’ll see me again,’ and by, ‘I’m going to the Father’?”
They kept asking, “What does ‘a little while’ mean? We don’t understand what he’s saying.”
Jesus knew they wanted to ask him about this, so he said, “Are you asking each other what I meant when I said, ‘In a little while you won’t see me, and then after a little while you’ll see me again’?
I’m telling you the truth: You’ll cry and grieve, but the world will celebrate. You’ll be sad, but your sadness will turn into joy.
When a woman is giving birth, she has pain because her time has come. But after the baby is born, she no longer remembers the suffering, because she’s happy a child has come into the world.
You’re sad now, but I’ll see you again. Then your hearts will be glad, and no one will take your joy away.
“When that day comes, you won’t ask me anything. I’m telling you the truth: The Father will give you whatever you ask in my name.
Until now, you haven’t asked for anything in my name. Ask, and you’ll receive, so your joy can be complete.
“I’ve been speaking to you in figures of speech. The time is coming when I won’t use figures of speech anymore; I’ll tell you plainly about the Father.
When that day comes, you’ll ask in my name. I’m not saying I’ll ask the Father on your behalf,
because the Father himself loves you. He loves you because you’ve loved me and believed I came from God.
I came from the Father and entered the world. Now I’m leaving the world and going back to the Father.”
His disciples said, “Now you’re speaking clearly, without figures of speech.
Now we know you know everything and don’t need anyone to question you. Because of this, we believe you came from God.”
Jesus answered, “Do you believe now?
The time is coming—in fact, it’s already here—when you’ll all scatter, each to your own place, and leave me alone. But I’m not alone, because the Father is with me.
I’ve told you these things so you can have peace in me. In this world you’ll have trouble. But take heart! I’ve overcome the world.”
After saying these things, Jesus looked up to heaven and prayed, “Father, the time has come. Glorify your Son so the Son may glorify you.
You gave him authority over all people, so he can give eternal life to everyone you’ve given him.
And this is eternal life: that they know you, the only true God, and Jesus Christ, the one you sent.
I glorified you here on earth by finishing the work you gave me to do.
Now, Father, glorify me in your presence with the glory I had with you before the world began.
“I have made your name known to the people you gave me from the world. They belonged to you, and you gave them to me. They’ve kept your word.
Now they know that everything you gave me comes from you.
I gave them the words you gave me. They accepted them and truly understood that I came from you. They believed you sent me.
I’m praying for them. I’m not praying for the world, but for those you gave me, because they belong to you.
Everything that belongs to me belongs to you, and everything that belongs to you belongs to me. I’m glorified through them.
“I’m no longer in the world, but they’re still in the world while I’m coming to you. Holy Father, protect them by your name—the name you gave me—so they may be one, just as we are one.
While I was with them, I protected them by your name, the name you gave me. I guarded them, and none was lost except the one doomed to destruction, so Scripture would be fulfilled.
Now I’m coming to you. I’m saying these things while I’m still in the world so they may have my joy made complete in themselves.
I’ve given them your word, and the world has hated them because they don’t belong to the world, just as I don’t belong to the world.
I’m not asking you to take them out of the world, but to protect them from the evil one.
They don’t belong to the world, just as I don’t belong to the world.
Set them apart by the truth. Your word is truth.
Just as you sent me into the world, I’ve sent them into the world.
For their sake, I set myself apart, so they too may truly be set apart.
“I’m not praying only for these disciples. I’m also praying for those who will believe in me because of their message,
so they may all be one. Father, just as you are in me and I am in you, may they also be in us, so the world may believe you sent me.
I’ve given them the glory you gave me, so they may be one just as we are one—
I in them and you in me—so they may be completely united. Then the world will know you sent me and loved them just as you loved me.
“Father, I want those you gave me to be with me where I am, so they can see the glory you gave me, because you loved me before the world was created.
Righteous Father, the world hasn’t known you, but I know you. These disciples know you sent me.
I’ve made your name known to them, and I’ll keep making it known, so the love you have for me may be in them, and I may be in them.”
After saying this, Jesus crossed the Kidron Valley with his disciples and entered a garden.
Judas, the one who betrayed him, knew that place well. Jesus often met there with his disciples.
So Judas arrived with a troop of soldiers and officers sent by the chief priests and Pharisees. They brought lanterns, torches, and weapons.
Jesus knew everything that was about to happen to him. He stepped forward and asked them, “Who are you looking for?”
They answered, “Jesus of Nazareth.” Jesus said, “I am he.” Judas, the one betraying him, was standing with them.
When Jesus said, “I am he,” they stepped back and fell to the ground.
So Jesus asked them again, “Who are you looking for?” They said, “Jesus of Nazareth.”
Jesus answered, “I told you I am he. If you’re looking for me, let the others go.”
This happened so the words he had spoken would come true: “I have not lost anyone you gave me.”
Simon Peter had a sword. He drew it, struck the high priest’s servant, and cut off his right ear. The servant’s name was Malchus.
Jesus told Peter, “Put your sword away. Shouldn’t I drink the cup the Father has given me?”
Then the soldiers, their commander, and the officers from the Jewish authorities arrested Jesus and tied him up.
First they took him to Annas, the father-in-law of Caiaphas, who was high priest that year.
Caiaphas was the one who had advised the Jewish authorities that it would be better for one man to die for the people.
Simon Peter followed Jesus, along with another disciple. That disciple was known to the high priest, so he went with Jesus into the high priest’s courtyard.
Peter stayed outside by the gate. The other disciple, who was known to the high priest, went back out, spoke to the woman guarding the gate, and brought Peter inside.
The woman guarding the gate asked Peter, “You’re one of this man’s disciples too, aren’t you?” He said, “I’m not.”
The servants and officers had made a charcoal fire because it was cold, and they stood around warming themselves. Peter was there too, warming himself with them.
The high priest questioned Jesus about his disciples and what he taught.
Jesus answered, “I’ve spoken openly to everyone. I always taught in synagogues and in the temple, where the people gather. I never said anything in secret.
Why question me? Ask the people who heard me what I said. They know what I taught.”
When Jesus said this, one of the officers standing nearby slapped him. “Is that how you answer the high priest?” he said.
Jesus replied, “If I said something wrong, tell them what was wrong. But if I spoke the truth, why did you hit me?”
Then Annas sent Jesus, still tied up, to Caiaphas the high priest.
Simon Peter was still standing there, warming himself. They asked him, “You’re not one of his disciples too, are you?” He denied it: “I’m not.”
One of the high priest’s servants, a relative of the man whose ear Peter had cut off, said, “Didn’t I see you with him in the garden?”
Peter denied it again. Right then, a rooster crowed.

They took Jesus from Caiaphas to the governor’s headquarters. It was early morning. They didn’t go inside, because they didn’t want to become ceremonially unclean; they still wanted to eat the Passover meal.
So Pilate came outside to them and asked, “What charge are you bringing against this man?”
They answered, “If he weren’t a criminal, we wouldn’t have handed him over to you.”
Pilate said, “Take him yourselves and judge him by your own law.” The Jewish authorities replied, “We aren’t allowed to execute anyone.”
This happened to fulfill what Jesus had said about the kind of death he would die.
Pilate went back inside the headquarters, called Jesus over, and asked, “Are you the King of the Jews?”
Jesus answered, “Are you asking that on your own, or did someone tell you that about me?”
Pilate replied, “Am I Jewish? Your own people and the chief priests handed you over to me. What have you done?”
Jesus answered, “My Kingdom doesn’t come from this world. If it did, my servants would fight so I wouldn’t be handed over to the Jewish authorities. But my Kingdom doesn’t come from here.”

Pilate said, “So you are a king?” Jesus answered, “You say I am a king. I was born for this, and I came into the world for this: to testify to the truth. Everyone who belongs to the truth listens to my voice.”
Pilate asked, “What is truth?” Then he went back outside to the Jewish authorities and said, “I find no reason to charge him.
But you have a custom that I release one prisoner to you at Passover. Do you want me to release the King of the Jews?”
They shouted back, “Not him! Give us Barabbas!” Barabbas was a robber.
Pilate took Jesus and had him whipped.
The soldiers twisted thorn branches into a crown, put it on his head, and dressed him in a purple robe.
They kept mocking him: “Long live the King of the Jews!” Then they kept slapping him.
Pilate went outside again and told them, “I’m bringing him out so you can see for yourselves that I find no reason to charge him.”
Jesus came out wearing the thorn crown and purple robe. Pilate said, “Look at the man.”
When the chief priests and their officers saw him, they shouted, “Crucify him! Crucify him!” Pilate said, “Take him and crucify him yourselves. I find no reason to charge him.”
The Jewish authorities answered, “We have a law. By our law he must die, because he claimed to be the Son of God.”
When Pilate heard that, he became even more afraid.
He went back inside the governor’s headquarters and asked Jesus, “Where are you from?” But Jesus didn’t answer.
Pilate said, “You won’t speak to me? Don’t you know I have authority to release you and authority to crucify you?”
Jesus answered, “You would have no authority over me at all unless it had been given to you from above. So the one who handed me over to you carries the greater sin.”
After that, Pilate kept trying to release Jesus. But the Jewish authorities shouted, “If you release this man, you’re no friend of Caesar! Anyone who makes himself a king is opposing Caesar!”
When Pilate heard them, he brought Jesus outside and sat on the judgment seat at a place called the Pavement, Gabbatha in Hebrew.
It was the Passover Preparation Day, around the sixth hour. Pilate said to the Jewish authorities, “Here is your King!”
They shouted, “Get rid of him! Get rid of him! Crucify him!” Pilate asked, “Should I crucify your King?” The chief priests answered, “We have no king except Caesar!”
So Pilate handed Jesus over to them to be crucified. They took him away.
Jesus carried his own cross to the place called the Place of a Skull—Golgotha in Hebrew.
There they crucified him, with two others, one on each side and Jesus in the middle.
